goal.what: Whoever builds or changes Lane, a person or an AI, makes each part of Lane without hesitating, on the same thinking as every other part, so that the parts together hold a plugin's subagents to the rules of their steps and to the order its developer AI sets, and Lane stays easy to read and to change.
grounds: plugins/turn/core/domain/best-practices/architecture.json goal: "Whoever builds or changes the product, a person or an AI, makes each part without hesitating, on the same thinking as every other part. Together, the parts then deliver the UX. The product stays easy to read and to change."
plugins/lane/README.md:3-4: "Lane is a Claude Code plugin that holds the subagents of your plugin to the rules of their steps and to the order that you set for them."

questions.what: For each step of the UX's scenarios, can the developer name the one way of using the product at its edge that carries it?
Having read the opening, can the developer say how the product delivers its UX, as one idea that every part carries out?
For anything the user stories need decided, can the developer point to the one role that decides it?
Starting on a role, can the developer begin without choosing for themselves what kind of thing it is and what it is made with?
When one developer makes the role that writes a data and another makes the role that reads it, do both join it to the other data the same way?
For each user story, can the developer follow it from the user's first request to its end, knowing at each step which role acts and what data it hands on?
Of any user story, role or data, can the developer tell which objective of the UX needs it?
When two developers of different parts meet a case the document does not name, does a principle's reason lead both to the same decision?
Setting the product up from nothing, can the developer put each role where it runs and each data where it is kept, and start the product, without asking anyone?
Making or changing a role or a data, can the developer find the one place its files belong?
Asked whether anything in the product goes untested, can the developer answer, for each deployment unit, which levels of test cover it, how heavily, and why a level is missing?
Writing a test at one level, can the developer do it without deciding for themselves what to run real, what to stand in with a double, what to cover and when it passes?
When the unit and architecture tests pass, can the developer be sure the product does what this document says, leaving ux only to confirm the UX?
Following a principle while building a part, does the developer find every figure, list and table asking the same of that part, so they never have to choose which to follow?
When the developer doubts a choice the document makes, can they tell what would be lost by taking the other way?
When the developer changes how a role works inside, while the UX and the principles stay, does every line of the document still hold?

decisions.what: Who reads the document, and which names does it give Lane's things?
decisions.decided: A developer, a person or an AI, who builds or changes Lane. The document uses the UX's and the README's names: developer AI, subagent, orchestrator, rule, route, result, the check script and the result script; the example plugin is changelog with lead, writer and reviewer. It says once, where it first names a rule, that Lane's code and user docs call a rule a lane and the check script the guard. It names no other plugin.
grounds: dev/lane/ux.md:3-4: "Lane's user is the developer AI, an AI that builds a Claude Code plugin whose subagents work in numbered steps."
plugins/lane/README.md:120-121: "Lane's output and documents call a rule a lane, and its check a hook."

decisions.what: How does Lane deliver its UX, as one idea?
decisions.decided: Lane turns each rule and route that the developer AI approves into a sentence in a step and a check of that sentence, and puts the checks into the developer AI's plugin as the check script, with the result script beside it. On a run, Claude Code runs the check script on each hook event, so the plugin's subagents meet the same sentence in their step and in each stop, and the orchestrator is told each start from the results the result script gave. The opening links the UX for what this gives.
grounds: architecture.json Q2 Practice thinking: "The opening says how the product turns what the user brings into what the UX promises. It says this in one idea seen from above, with none of a part's inner workings."
architecture.json Q2 Practice step: "Link the UX instead of repeating it."

plugins/lane/README.md: "How it works" figure: proposes the rules and the routes; writes the sentence of each rule into its step; copies into your plugin; stops a break and shows the sentence again; tells which subagent to start next

decisions.what: Which principles of the plugin best practice does Lane take, and which not?
decisions.decided: Lane takes: What a machine can see of the work; No check passes what it did not check; The guard tells each role its steps again; Where a plugin writes its files; Asking for what lies outside the work (in what it tells a stopped subagent); The caller approves what is theirs; Python 3.9 and the standard library; Code kept once. It does not take the principles of a plugin with an orchestrator and roles, nor An entry points to its part, Languages and Learning from each run, as Lane has no role, skill or agent of its own and talks with no person: the developer AI runs lay.py itself, and the check script runs inside the developer AI's plugin. It departs from The core apart from Claude Code in where its core lies (D17).
grounds: architecture.json Q8 Practice step: "Link the principles of the architecture this one is built on, and write only what this product adds or changes."
dev/plugin-best-practice.md:82-83: "A plugin takes the principles its requirements call for, and its architecture names the ones it takes."

decisions.what: What principles does Lane add, each with its rule and its reason?
decisions.decided: Eight, each a rule every part follows and a reason tied to a key result: The check shows the step again (KR1.1, a call stopped and then done another way); One wording for the step and the check (lanes/ alone makes the sentence); What was approved is what runs (the check script takes rules and routes only from what lay.py write wrote, and holds them to the checks lay.py print made); Lane knows no plugin (absent: a line naming another plugin; KR1.1 and KR2.1, Lane cannot hold a rule or an order); The check judges only what Claude Code documents (absent: reading a subagent's words, a shell command taken apart, or Claude Code's session record); A call that cannot be checked is stopped; Claude Code's own means first; The plugin needs nothing from Lane. Three of them say what must be absent as a rule.
grounds: architecture.json Q8 Practice thinking: "A principle is a rule that every part meeting the same decision follows the same way. The principle says what it is there for, so a developer can carry it to a case it does not name."
architecture.json Q8 Practice step: "Write as a rule also what must be absent, such as a dependency no role may have."
dev/lane/ux.md:15-18: "it breaks a rule, is stopped, and is then done another way; [...] Lane cannot hold the rule, so the developer AI writes a check of its own or leaves the rule unchecked."

decisions.what: Do two developers of different parts reach the same decision on a case no rule names?
decisions.decided: Tried on the case of a new hook event that Claude Code adds: the developer of hook.py and the developer of guard.py both stop a call of the event that cannot be read (A call that cannot be checked is stopped), and both read only its documented fields (The check judges only what Claude Code documents). Tried on a plugin whose list of items is in a table: both reach an adapter, not a new type of rule (Lane knows no plugin). The reasons hold as written.
grounds: architecture.json Q8 Practice step: "Take a case no rule names, and have two developers of different parts decide it from the reasons alone. Where they differ, sharpen the reason."

decisions.what: Which user stories carry the UX's steps?
decisions.decided: S1 lay.py print (O1 and O2: the rules or routes, the steps as they will read). S2 lay.py write (O1 and O2: approves them, the steps written). S3 a subagent with rules on a run, as writer (O1: starts writer, each tool call let through or stopped with the sentence of its step, ends with both rules kept). S4 a subagent gives its result and ends (O2: ends with written, ends with more or good). S5 the orchestrator is told each start, as lead (O2: starts writer and reviewer as the routes say, ends with the reviewed entries). Off the main path: S6 runs at once of one subagent (KR2.1), S7 lay.py up after Lane is updated (KR1.1, KR2.1). The held command, the value given for a run and the call that cannot be checked are branches of S3, not stories, as each meets Lane by the same tool call.

decisions.what: Does every story, role and data reach an objective?
decisions.decided: Each story names its UX steps or key result. Each role and data is reached by a story's sequence. Answer, the subagent's reply, goes from the components figure: Lane never reads it, and no sequence of Lane hands it on. The held command stays, as a branch of S3: without it a rule that needs a person's approval is one Lane cannot hold (KR1.1). The value given for a run and the adapter stay for the same reason. lay.py up stays: without it a fault fixed in Lane never reaches a plugin's copy (KR1.1, KR2.1).

decisions.what: Which roles and stores are there, each with its type and technology?
decisions.decided: Roles of Lane: lay.py [command line · Python 3.9]; proposal.py [module · Python 3.9]; the check script [hook script · Python 3.9], made of hook.py [hook entry], guard.py, lanes/, called.py, routes.py and ports.py [modules]; result.py, the result script [command line · Python 3.9]. Outside Lane: Developer AI [AI · Claude Code], Subagent [AI · Claude Code], Operator [person or AI], Claude Code [CLI], Adapter [script · Python 3, the developer AI's]. Stores: Proposal [files · JSON, Python], which holds the proposal with its adapters and their test cases; Plugin files [files · Markdown, JSON]; Calls kept [files · JSONL].

decisions.what: Which arrows does the components figure draw?
decisions.decided: Each arrow says what one role does to another with the data it hands on: the developer AI writes the Proposal and runs lay.py; lay.py has proposal.py check the Proposal, has lanes/ make each sentence, writes the Plugin files, removes the Proposal and has Claude Code validate the plugin; proposal.py reads the test cases, has ports.py run the adapter on each, and has lanes/ and routes.py check the rules and the routes, so ports.py alone runs an adapter; Claude Code runs hook.py on each event and result.py on the subagent's call; hook.py hands the event to guard.py and gets a Decision back; guard.py runs each check in lanes/, reads and keeps calls through called.py, asks routes.py the next start, has ports.py read a text, and reads the Plugin files; ports.py runs the Adapter; called.py reads and writes Calls kept; result.py reads the routes in the Plugin files; Claude Code shows the operator the replies, the permission prompts and Lane's messages, and the operator runs the plugin and answers the prompts. guard.py, not hook.py, asks routes.py, as guard.py alone decides what an event gets. result.py no longer reads through ports.py, as it checks only the result. A legend explains every shape and tag.

decisions.what: Which role alone decides each point the stories need?
decisions.decided: lay.py: what is written where in the plugin; nothing else writes there. proposal.py: whether a proposal can be laid. lanes/: for each type of rule, its sentence, what it is given and what breaks it. hook.py: the form of Claude Code's hook input and output, and which events belong to a subagent with rules. guard.py: which checks run on an event, and what the subagent, the orchestrator and the operator are told. called.py: what is kept of each run and how the runs of one subagent join. routes.py: whether routes can be followed, the next start, and the result of runs at once. ports.py: how a text of the plugin is read into Port JSON. result.py: whether the result a subagent gives is one it may give. Written beside the figure, apart from the choices.

decisions.what: Which data does the data model draw, and how do they join?
decisions.decided: The data model keeps its sixteen data: Proposal, Rule, Route, Order of results, Adapter, Test case, Port JSON, Subagent file, Step, Hook entry, Rules laid, Event, Decision, Kept call, Run value and Result, each by its name alone with no fields. The relation between Rules laid and Subagent file is named "lets run at once", so lay.py, which writes it from fan_out, and routes.py, which reads it, keep it the same way.

decisions.what: Which sequences are drawn, and how?
decisions.decided: One Mermaid sequence for each of S1 to S7, with the participants named as in Components and each message labelled with the data it hands on, named as in the data model. S3 draws the loop of the UX's O1 with each branch of a tool call: let through, stopped with the sentence of its step, held for the person, needing a value given for the run, and unable to be checked. S5 draws the orchestrator's end: let end when no start is due, kept going once while one is due. Each step runs along an arrow of Components. No message holds a semicolon.

decisions.what: Which choices would a developer question, and what does each cost?
decisions.decided: Beside Components: the checks as entries of the plugin's hooks.json acting by agent_type, over hooks in the subagent's file; Lane's code put into the plugin, over run from Lane; commands matched whole, over a shell command taken apart; called.py keeping calls itself, over Claude Code's session record; the result from a run of the result script, over the subagent's reply; the adapter as a script, over a module. Beside the sequences: subagents with rules in the background; the next start told as context; the orchestrator kept going once, then let end with the operator told; only the subagents in fan_out run several at once. Beside Deployment: the kept calls in the temporary folder; a link in this marketplace and a copy elsewhere. Beside Directory: Lane's core in hooks/lane/core/domain/. Beside the test table: each weight. Each says what it beat, why, and what it costs.
grounds: architecture.json Q15 Practice thinking: "A choice that a developer would question, such as a technology, a tool or a unit's weight, carries why it beat the other way and what it costs. These stand beside the figure or table that shows the choice."

decisions.what: What leaves the document, as it holds how a role works inside?
decisions.decided: Out, as the user docs already say them for users: how a value is quoted (shlex), how a dependency's folder is matched, the 3-second wait for a start, the status names of an Agent call, PostToolUseFailure, how runs at once are counted and replaced, and what a step's result command looks like; the document links plugins/lane/docs/lanes.md and routes.md where a reader needs them. Out, as they are inside a role: the helper modules of lay.py and guard.py in the tree, the file name of each run's kept calls, and the record of each try of Claude Code with its version and date, which goes beside the double of Claude Code in dev/lane/testing.py. The paths of the architecture tests follow the branches of the sequences, not a role's cases.
grounds: architecture.json Q16 Practice thinking: "The document holds only what stays while the UX and the principles stay. It leaves how each role works inside to where the role is built."

architecture.json Q16 Practice step: "Imagine a change to how a role works inside, such as its steps, a value it uses or a data's fields, that leaves the UX and the principles as they are. Mark each line the change would make untrue."

decisions.what: Where does each role run and each data lie, and how does Lane start?
decisions.decided: Two environments, which may be one computer: the developer AI's computer holds the lay.py process (lay.py, proposal.py, lanes/, routes.py, ports.py), the adapter process, .lane/<yyyymmdd>-<plugin>/ with the Proposal, the Adapter and the Test cases, and the plugin's folder; the computer where the plugin runs holds the hook process (the check script), the adapter process, the result process (result.py), the temporary folder with Calls kept, and the installed plugin with Lane's code. Outside: the marketplace on GitHub, and Claude Code. Start: the developer AI installs Lane as the README says and runs lay.py; Claude Code starts the check script through the plugin's hook entries.

decisions.what: Where do the files of each role and data lie?
decisions.decided: A tree with one line for each role and data: scripts/lay.py; hooks/lane/ with hook.py, result.py and core/domain/ holding proposal.py, guard.py, lanes/, called.py, routes.py and ports.py; the docs; dev/lane/ with tests/unit, tests/architecture and tests/ux; and, as Lane lays and keeps them, .lane/<yyyymmdd>-<plugin>/, the temporary folder's lane/, and in the plugin agents/, hooks/hooks.json, hooks/lanes.json, hooks/adapters/ and hooks/lane/. The modules inside a role are left out.
grounds: architecture.json Q10 Practice step: "Keep the folders and files that hold a role or a data, and leave out what lies inside each."
architecture.json Q10 Practice step: "Check that each role and each data stands on one line."

decisions.what: Where does Lane's core lie?
decisions.decided: In hooks/lane/core/domain/, not in core/ at the plugin's root as The core apart from Claude Code has it: lay.py lays hooks/lane/ into each plugin whole, by one link or one copy, and a core outside it would need a second. The cost: the core lies apart from where the plugin best practice puts every other plugin's core. Lane has no roles of its own, so it has no core/roles/.
grounds: dev/plugin-best-practice.md:88: "An entry holds only the form Claude Code fixes, and hands the job to its part in core/."

decisions.what: Which levels test each deployment unit, how heavily, and which unit has no row?
decisions.decided: A test table as an SVG, rows the lay.py, hook and result processes, columns unit, architecture and ux. Unit: unittest, with coverage, Cosmic Ray and Hypothesis confirming, ●●●. Architecture: unittest with the processes run real and doubles of Claude Code and the AIs, ●●●, each story's sequence from start to end. ux: a trial on Opus, ●○○, the scenario of O1 or O2. The adapter process has no row: an adapter is the developer AI's code, and Lane's running of it is tested in the lay.py and hook rows. Lane has no prompt of its own, so it has no trial at unit.

decisions.what: What does each level run real, stand in with a double, cover, and pass on?
decisions.decided: The rules link the plugin best practice's Test and write only what Lane adds. Unit: the classes of each type of rule (a call it allows, one that breaks it, one it cannot check), each for a subagent with rules and one without; a double of Claude Code is each event as JSON in the documented fields; a double of claude is a script on PATH. Architecture: lay.py, the check script run by the hooks' commands in sh, result.py and the files lay.py lays run real; doubles of Claude Code, of the developer AI, of the subagents and of the person; one test for each path of each sequence, listed in a table looked up by row. Each double gives only what its part's contract allows, checked by the check the part's unit tests make; a double of Claude Code sends what the hooks reference documents, or what a recorded try showed, recorded beside the double. ux: a developer AI on Opus stands in for Lane's user, given an intent written before the run and never shown to Lane; it writes the proposal, lays it, and runs changelog with an ask that invites a break; 3 runs of 3 must meet the objective; the trial measures each key result. A fault a higher level finds is first tested at the level that must catch it.

decisions.what: Does every figure, list and table ask the same of each part as the principles?
decisions.decided: Read each part against each principle: no figure draws a read of Claude Code's record or of a subagent's reply (The check judges only what Claude Code documents); every arrow that writes into the plugin starts at lay.py (What was approved is what runs); the deployment puts Lane's code inside the plugin, never a call back to Lane (The plugin needs nothing from Lane); lanes/ is the one role both lay.py and guard.py use for a sentence (One wording); each sequence's could-not-check branch stops the call and tells the operator (A call that cannot be checked is stopped).
grounds: architecture.json Q14 Practice step: "Read each part against each principle that rules it. Where a line breaks the principle, change the part, or the principle and its reason, until the two say the same."
